channel.title: Updated · all tabs
channel.description: Daily news and research, explained: every tab

item.title: China's space station cools a cloud of atoms to a record 9.7 picokelvin
item.description: Researchers aboard China's Tiangong station cooled about 20,000 rubidium atoms to an equivalent 9.7 picokelvin, about four times below the previous record, and watched the cloud expand for seven seconds. (Phys.org, Chinese Academy of Sciences)

item.title: The Arctic polar vortex is breaking down weeks earlier than ever observed
item.description: Meteorologists say the stratospheric polar vortex is weakening in early November, the earliest disruption on record, but the cause and any effect on winter weather remain uncertain. (BBC Weather, Phys.org (AFP))

item.title: Mantle currents may have helped carve the Great Unconformity, geologists' biggest gap in the rock record
item.description: Simulations of mantle convection over the past billion years suggest slow uplift of continents, followed by glacial scouring, helped create the Great Unconformity. (Phys.org (University of Wollongong), Ars Technica)

item.title: Three-way circulation–soil moisture–temperature feedbacks amplify the most extreme mid-latitudinal heat waves
item.description: A three-way feedback between drying soils, high-pressure systems and heat appears to make the most extreme midlatitude heat waves about 10% hotter, and warming makes the trigger threshold easier to cross. (Yinglin Tian, Jiangong Liu, Yu Huang et al. · Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research; International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis; Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology)

item.title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
item.description: Shot-noise measurements in a bismuth-based cuprate suggest the pseudogap energy equals the energy at which electrons begin pairing, tying a mysterious phase to superconductivity's building block. (Jiasen Niu, Maialen Ortego Larrazabal, Thomas Gozlinski et al. · Utrecht University; Leiden University; Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich)

item.title: Quantum gas microscopy of three-flavor Hubbard systems
item.description: Researchers built the first tunable three-component Hubbard system from ultracold atoms and imaged it atom by atom, observing a Mott insulator and competing magnetic correlations. (Jirayu Mongkolkiattichai, Liyu Liu, Sohail Dasgupta et al. · University of Hamburg; Rice University)

item.title: US hiring surprises at 165,000 jobs while Canada's labour market weakens, with unemployment at 4.1% and 6.7%
item.description: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October versus about 65,000 expected, while Canada lost 4,700 jobs and its unemployment rate rose to 6.7%, widening the gap between the two labour markets. (Statistics Canada, Associated Press via The Globe and Mail, Reuters via The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Canada's 2026 budget moves bank anti-money-laundering supervision to OSFI and proposes tax simplifications
item.description: Ottawa's budget shifts supervision of banks' anti-money-laundering work from FinTRAC to OSFI, offers modest corporate tax simplification, and a follow-on reform loosens temporary foreign worker limits. (Budget 2026, Government of Canada, The Globe and Mail, The Globe and Mail, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: The Effects of Monetary Policy on Macroeconomic Expectations: High-Frequency Evidence from Prediction Markets
item.description: Using minute-by-minute prices of Kalshi prediction-market contracts, the authors find macro expectations respond to Fed announcements as standard theory predicts, with little or no "Fed information effect". (Eric T. Swanson, Wang Renxuan, Yanbin Wu)

item.title: Google releases Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with 15-second video and a 30% lower price
item.description: Google made Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available, with native 15-second video, multi-turn conversational editing, better reference adherence and a price of $0.07 per second at 720p, down 30%. (Google)

item.title: OpenAI reportedly raises another $11 billion, valuing it at $1.25 trillion
item.description: Bloomberg reports OpenAI has raised $11 billion so far in a round at a $1.25 trillion valuation, with the total expected to reach about $20 billion, well below the $30 billion first sought. (TechCrunch, The Verge)

item.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
item.description: VFlash predicts a whole bounding box or robot trajectory in one forward pass instead of token by token, cutting trajectory errors versus autoregressive decoding while running far faster. (Yu-Cheng Chou, Shihao Wang, Jin Huang et al. · NVIDIA)

item.title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
item.description: WebHarbor rebuilds 153 real websites as offline, resettable Docker environments with 3,518 tasks, and a 4B web agent trained only there matches or beats one trained on live sites. (Zhaoyang Wang, Qianhui Wu, Boyu Gou et al. · Microsoft, Tongji University)

item.title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?
item.description: Multi-turn RL helps LLM agents mainly by improving recovery from errors over long horizons, not single-step decisions, so its gains shrink when the turn budget is tight; mixing budgets in training narrows that gap. (Kejian Zhu, Zhuoran Jin, Shangqing Tu et al.)

item.title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
item.description: Across many modalities the best model varies by input, but learned routers beat the best single model only slightly; routing's reliable win is cost, averaging 8.82 times better efficiency. (Pengfei Zhou, Yixing Ma, Hexin Wang et al. · National University of Singapore, University of California Berkeley, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)

item.title: RoboColosseum: Evaluating Physical Intelligence at Scale In-The-Wild
item.description: RoboColosseum runs blinded pairwise robot trials across 124 sites and finds frontier chat agents rival specialized robot policies, while rankings vary across tasks, robots and evaluation tracks. (Tan Sang Nguyen, Yi Ru Wang, Shailesh Shailesh et al. · National University of Singapore, Hugging Face, Singapore Embodied AI Centre)

item.title: Chainalysis says hackers obtained credentials and live tokens for all of its users
item.description: Chainalysis, whose tools trace cryptocurrency flows, now says names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for every user were exposed, widening an incident first described as limited. (BleepingComputer, Ars Technica)

item.title: DigiCert says a 16-month exposure of an internal system let an outsider read customer identity documents
item.description: DigiCert says a server migration left an internal archive reachable from the internet from February 2025, and an unauthorized account read some customer records in June and July 2026. (The Register, The Record)

item.title: Fox completes its $22 billion acquisition of Roku, five months after announcing it
item.description: Fox closed its $22 billion purchase of Roku, which reaches more than 100 million households, far earlier than the first-half-2027 completion the companies had projected. (TechCrunch, Engadget)

item.title: AST SpaceMobile plans its own medium-lift rocket, backed by a $1.3 billion Firefly engine deal
item.description: The direct-to-phone satellite company says it will build Blacklift, a 20-ton-class rocket, and has committed $1.3 billion to Firefly for engines, a license and engineering support. (Ars Technica, Firefly Aerospace newsroom (headline))

item.title: FaultScope: A software package for fast error attribution in quantum error correction
item.description: FaultScope is an open-source simulator that estimates how much each noisy component contributes to logical errors in quantum error correction, at under 1% extra runtime in tests. (Yuguo Shao, Zhenyu Chen, Ningfeng Wang et al. · Yau Mathematical Sciences Center, Tsinghua University; Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications; Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University)

item.title: FDA grants accelerated approval to a subcutaneous antibody for previously treated head and neck cancer
item.description: The FDA granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro for recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma after chemotherapy and immunotherapy, based on a 42% response rate in 102 patients. (FDA, Johnson & Johnson (OrigAMI-4 results release))

item.title: A hair and 1,000 seeds from a Siberian tomb give the oldest directly dated evidence of cannabis intoxication
item.description: Archaeologists found about 1,000 cannabis seeds and hair carrying a breakdown product of THC in a Scythian princely tomb in Siberia, dated to the early eighth century B.C., in a study in Science. (University of Bern, New Scientist, Scientific American)

item.title: The deep Earth origin of the Great Unconformity
item.description: Models of slow mantle flow suggest continents rose for hundreds of millions of years and then sank, which would erase and then bury the rock record behind the Great Unconformity. (Santosh Dhungana, Nicolas Flament)

item.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
item.description: A physics-based model of Webb's camera, tuned with the gradient descent used to train neural networks, cuts noise in exoplanet images and revealed a planet that had gone unseen at one wavelength. (Rodrigo Ferrer-Chavez, Jason J. Wang, Katherine L. Bouman et al.)

item.title: Wall Street's AI-driven rout deepens after the midterms and spreads across Asia
item.description: US stocks fell sharply on Thursday as investors feared Democratic control of Congress could slow the AI buildout, and the losses spread to Japan, South Korea and Taiwan on Friday. (The Guardian (live, Nov 6), The Guardian (Nov 4), The Globe and Mail (Reuters))

item.title: Tesla says it will stop making the Cybertruck next year to make room for the Cybercab
item.description: Elon Musk said Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production in 2027, using the factory space for its two-seat Cybercab robotaxi after years of weak sales. (BBC News, TechCrunch)

item.title: Aggregate-Surplus Maximizing Monetary Policy
item.description: A new NBER paper finds that when households differ in labor-market frictions, a central bank maximizing everyone's joint surplus should weight output stabilization about 37 percent more than inflation, compared with the standard model. (David Baqaee, Ariel Burstein, Joao Guerreiro)

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, a cybersecurity model rated "Critical" on its Preparedness Framework
item.description: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber to vetted defenders, claiming better exploit-finding and far fewer out-of-scope actions, and its Preparedness Framework rates it "Critical" for cybersecurity. (The Verge, TechCrunch)

item.title: Anthropic lets Claude read your bank accounts with a new Personal Finance feature
item.description: Anthropic launched a beta Personal Finance tool that links Claude to bank and card accounts through Plaid with read-only access, following a similar ChatGPT feature from May. (The Verge, TechCrunch)

item.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
item.description: ToolSpace builds agent training tasks from how real tools are chained in execution traces, producing cross-service workflows that lift open models toward frontier tool-use scores. (Guanting Dong, Zhichao Sun, Xinyu Yang et al. · Renmin University of China, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University)

item.title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
item.description: Merging several specialist models into one with on-policy distillation reaches near-teacher scores on training tasks yet loses ground on harder or combined tasks, unless supervision is also broadened. (Yichen Wang, Yufa Zhou, Siqi Zhu et al. · University of Chicago, Duke University, UIUC)

item.title: Reinforcement Learning Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement
item.description: Fine-tuning a generalist robot policy with value-based reinforcement learning across many tasks improves it on unseen objects and scenes, which single-task fine-tuning does not. (Michal Korniak, Marco Bagatella, Ralf Römer et al. · ETH Zurich, MPI for Intelligent Systems, Technical University of Munich)

item.title: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably
item.description: PEARL trains a language model to recover from partly misaligned starts, making removal of a bad behavior far more resistant to later fine-tuning than standard supervised or reinforcement learning fixes. (Luxi He, Pengcheng Jiang, Jifan Zhang et al. · Princeton University, UIUC, Thinking Machines Lab)

item.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
item.description: Speculative decoding is lossless in distribution but not in numerical precision, and the authors train the draft model to disagree at key decision points to improve long-horizon coding agents. (Hongyin Luo, Wei Fang, Lijie Yang et al. · Subconscious)

item.title: OpenSSH patch fixes "*sshole", a ten-year-old login bypass on musl-based Linux systems
item.description: OpenSSH 10.6p2 fixes a flaw, present since 2016, that lets an oversized password log in to accounts meant to refuse passwords on musl-based Linux systems such as Alpine. (BleepingComputer, The Register)

item.title: Blue Origin pushes the next New Glenn launch into January 2027 after May launchpad explosion
item.description: Blue Origin's CEO told staff the next New Glenn flight is now targeted for January 2027, after earlier hopes of launching before the end of this year. (Engadget, The Verge)

item.title: FAA begins replacing floppy-disk-based air traffic displays with a digital system at more than 400 facilities
item.description: The FAA says it will replace 1980s display systems that run on floppy disks with the digital E-IDS platform, targeting 435 sites by the end of 2028. (Engadget, FAA)

item.title: Beyond Sensitive APIs: Detecting Access Control Flaws at Sensitive Callsites in Android Firmware
item.description: Callix, a tool that judges whether access checks are strong enough for a sensitive operation, found 819 vulnerable paths in pre-installed apps from ten Android vendors. (Haotian Deng, Meng Hao, Hanxiao Chen et al. · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China)

item.title: British health worker with Ebola flown home as the Congo outbreak passes 10,000 cases
item.description: A British healthcare worker infected in DR Congo is being evacuated to the UK, the first British case of an outbreak that has passed 10,000 confirmed cases and has no approved treatment. (The Guardian, ECDC)

item.title: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis
item.description: Researchers built the largest map yet of how essential genes interact in the tuberculosis bacterium, finding nearly 6,500 interactions that could guide new drug targets and antibiotic combinations. (Isaac J. Kresse, Natalie Y. Sayegh, Vanisha Munsamy-Govender et al. · Rockefeller University)

item.title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
item.description: A global analysis of 45 threats to more than 21,000 freshwater species finds farming, dams and agricultural runoff dominate, and that freshwater species face higher threat on average than land species. (Christophe Brabant, Laura Pollock, Jonas Geldmann et al. · McGill University)

item.title: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial
item.description: A large international randomized trial found no evidence that prone positioning or high-frequency oscillatory ventilation improves ventilator-free days in children with early, moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome. (Martha A Q Curley, Martin C J Kneyber, Ira M Cheifetz et al.)

item.title: NASA's Swift gamma-ray observatory ends its 22-year mission with a fiery re-entry
item.description: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, which tracked more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts, was predicted to fall out of orbit on 4 November after a failed rescue attempt, and NASA now lists it as having re-entered. (The Guardian, NASA)

item.title: A hidden companion star may be stirring Betelgeuse's atmosphere
item.description: Radio observations from the VLA and ALMA suggest a close companion star, Siwarha, distorts the atmosphere of the red supergiant Betelgeuse, which has otherwise recovered from its Great Dimming. (ScienceDaily (ALMA release), The Astronomical Journal)

item.title: Uranium cubes show Germany's last wartime reactor was far short of what it needed
item.description: A PNAS Nexus analysis of surviving uranium cubes and archives finds the B8 reactor would have needed 1,292 to 1,775 cubes, far more than the 664 used, contradicting Heisenberg's claim that it was nearly critical. (Ars Technica, PNAS Nexus)

item.title: Towards observing interstitial hydrogen in solution in metal lattices
item.description: Cryogenic atom probe tomography with deuterium tracers gives the first direct observation of hydrogen dissolved in the gaps between metal atoms, and shows the metal's makeup decides where it sits. (Chao Huang, Saiyu Liu, Wenting Lv et al. · University of Sydney)

item.title: Enigmatic HCl detections as a potential signature of igneous activity on Mars
item.description: Seasonal hydrogen chloride spikes above fresh fissures on Mars's Alba Mons suggest gas seeping from hot magma, a possible sign that Mars is dormant rather than dead. (Alexander Trokhimovskiy, Daniel Mège, Oleg Korablev et al. · Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences)

item.title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
item.description: Evidence of chirality in manganese telluride supports altermagnetism as a real third class of magnetism that sits between ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. (Daniel Jost, Resham Babu Regmi, Eder G. Lomeli et al. · SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory)

item.title: Bank of England raises its rate to 4%, the first increase in more than three years
item.description: The Bank of England voted 8-1 to lift Bank Rate to 4% from 3.75%, saying energy-driven inflation pressure in the pipeline is now strong enough to justify tighter policy. (Bank of England, BBC, BBC)

item.title: ECB wage tracker points to slightly firmer negotiated pay growth into 2027
item.description: The ECB's wage tracker shows negotiated wage growth of 2.7% in late 2026 and 2.8% in early 2027, a little higher than the 2.3% headline figure for 2026 as a whole. (European Central Bank)

item.title: US trade deficit narrows slightly to $105.0 billion in September as exports and imports both rise
item.description: The US goods and services trade deficit eased by $0.7 billion to $105.0 billion in September, though the three-month average deficit widened to $101.2 billion. (U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis)

item.title: Canada's trade surplus widens to a four-year high as gold and energy offset tariff-hit exports
item.description: Canada's September merchandise trade surplus widened to about C$5.4 billion, the highest since May 2022, but gold and oil hid a 5.6% drop in other exports hit by US tariffs. (Statistics Canada, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Demand-Driven Inflation
item.description: Giannone and Primiceri argue that unexpectedly strong demand, not supply shocks alone, drove the post-pandemic inflation surge in both the United States and the euro area. (Domenico Giannone, Giorgio Primiceri · Johns Hopkins University; Northwestern University)

item.title: Midterm results make the data-center backlash a political force that could slow AI buildout
item.description: US voters backed candidates and ballot measures that restrict data centers, and with Democrats winning Congress, new limits on the buildout behind AI are now more likely. (The Verge, TechCrunch, Wired)

item.title: Moonshot AI releases the weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 3T-class agentic model
item.description: Moonshot AI published open weights for Kimi K3.1 Pro, a natively multimodal agentic model with a one-million-token context window, post-trained from Kimi K3 with large-scale reinforcement learning. (Moonshot AI (Hugging Face model card))

item.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
item.description: IdeaTaste scores LLM-written research proposals against what a field actually published later, finding models match only about 18% of the human level on ideas. (Shanshan Zhong, Chen Xu, Jingjie Ning et al. · Carnegie Mellon University, Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence)

item.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
item.description: NEO-VLA drops the separate vision encoder from a robot policy and lets its action module read visual features from many backbone layers, beating encoder-based baselines on LIBERO. (Weichen Fan, Haiwen Diao, Penghao Wu et al. · MMLab@NTU)

item.title: You don't need long context
item.description: NVIDIA researchers show frontier models keep most of their accuracy on long-horizon and long-input tasks when forced to work in short contexts through frequent compaction. (Peter Belcak, Saurav Muralidharan, Jindong Jiang et al. · NVIDIA)

item.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
item.description: FrontierPhysics has 42 physicists turn their own research into 56 end-to-end tasks, and no AI agent configuration passes more than 46 of 168 attempts. (Bingran You, Wenjun Ke, Ria Rosenauer et al. · Multi-institution team of physicists (26 institutions))
